bug_semantics: When persistent proxy memory is enabled, the proxy used the client-controlled x-headroom-user-id header as the memory partition key without authenticating or binding that identifier to the caller. A reachable client could select another user's partition, disclose stored memory through search/context injection, and create, update, or delete records in that partition. The shipped compose deployment made the data plane network-reachable by binding 0.0.0.0 and publishing port 8787 without requiring a proxy token.
flaw_origin: Commit da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 is the smallest public-history BIC. It introduced proxy memory, read memory_user_id from x-headroom-user-id in headroom/proxy/server.py, and passed that untrusted value to memory search and tool-call read/write operations implemented by the newly added headroom/proxy/memory_handler.py. Its sole parent 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80 contains neither the header selector nor proxy memory handler. Later handler splits and OpenAI, Gemini, Responses, and WebSocket additions moved or copied the already-vulnerable identity selection and are not introducers.
ai_marker: absent — `git cat-file -p da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192` shows a single parent, human author and committer chopratejas <chopratejas@gmail.com>, and a complete message with no Co-Authored-By AI identity, bot identity, Generated-with/Made-with trailer, or other explicit AI attribution.
evidence: The assigned fix disagreement is the primary's fix_sha=1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0/direct_fix_sha=ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f versus the reviewer's use of 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 for both fields. The official GHSA page describes the vulnerable direct header reads and the resolve_memory_identity remediation, but lists affected and patched versions as Unknown, so the repository supplies the commit and release boundaries. `git cat-file -p 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0` shows that the landed PR #2207 object is a one-parent GitHub-authored squash on a3d9424de98c54cb5656d29a33de6fe673691aca. `git grep -n x-headroom-user-id a3d9424de98c54cb5656d29a33de6fe673691aca -- headroom/proxy/handlers` finds six vulnerable reads, while the 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 tree replaces every handler read with resolve_memory_identity and adds headroom/proxy/identity.py; therefore 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 is the landed fix_sha. For direct provenance, `git log --all --reverse -Sresolve_memory_identity --format='%H %P %s' -- headroom/proxy/identity.py headroom/proxy/handlers/anthropic.py headroom/proxy/handlers/gemini.py headroom/proxy/handlers/openai.py` starts at ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f, whose sole parent is b75999017fc060a4617077ef86c21ce3249d0842. A grep of that parent finds the six direct header reads, and the ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f diff creates identity.py and routes those sites through the resolver. The branch ancestry is ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f -> merge 6cf575e69756ee39c04817c47ab64a9bd9d70a32 -> refresh merge 839a12e0fdebe3ce44016d57a5a3590349138149 before the final squash. Those merges and the 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 squash are aggregate integration objects, not the first direct authoring object, so the primary's direct_fix_sha wins and the reviewer incorrectly conflated landed fix with direct fix. BIC checks: `git log --all --reverse -Sx-headroom-user-id -- headroom/proxy` starts at da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192; its raw object has sole parent 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80, and `git grep -n x-headroom-user-id 8c22a72715a328f1f7c3d4ba4a44516910192e80 -- headroom/proxy` exits 1 with no match. The BIC is not a merge, move, revert, import, or release aggregate and exposes no smaller squash-member SHA. Version checks: tags containing the BIC begin at v0.3.0, v0.2.15 has no selector, v0.36.0 still has all six direct reads, and tags containing landed fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 begin at v0.36.1 (tag commit 37faf2f24724370483b1819b0921c899791bedc7). Thus the repository-derived affected range is v0.3.0 through v0.36.0 and the first fixed release is v0.36.1.
reasoning: The vulnerability begins when an unauthenticated network header first becomes the persistent-memory tenant selector, so da743418584725e8b9c3315dc1aea7cf5e949192 is causal and minimal and its immediate parent proves absence. Propagation into later handlers does not replace that BIC. For the disputed fix provenance, both audits correctly identify 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 as the shipped mainline fix and v0.36.1 boundary, but only the primary preserves the distinct first direct remediation object: ac962fcce374739572c04e09269c12b9daeb457f first authored the resolver and replaced the vulnerable reads, whereas 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 is the later aggregate squash that landed the refreshed branch. The intervening merge/refinement objects are not substituted for the direct authoring commit. Finally, attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object; its human identities and trailer-free message contain no AI evidence. With the BIC, immediate-parent absence, direct and landed fixes, and release boundary all verified, the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
